I am an old woman, sixty years, and I work this small maize plot myself like I always did. The plot is very small, just a corner of my land, and I have no money to buy those fertilizer bags from the cooperative — one bag is too much for this little plot and the cash is not there. I will put the manure from my few animals on the soil like my mother taught me, use the seed I kept from last harvest, and pull the weeds with my own hands. The rain must come when it comes; I cannot bring water to this plot.
